name: The Oracle (Orantha Cornelius — Suspected)
title: The Metaphysical Custodian of Raventree Manor
race: Unknown — Possibly Toad, Possibly Something That Was Once A Toad
status: Active — Location: Fracture Atrium, Corvinarus Sanctum — Intentions: Unclear, As Always
affiliation: House Corvinarus / Raventree Manor / The Timeline Itself (Self-Appointed)
summary: The Oracle is not a person. It is a role, a function, a custodian of bleeding timelines wearing the face of whoever was convenient when the job needed filling. It — he, she, they, Waluigi cannot determine the correct pronoun and the Oracle has not volunteered one — has survived a bullet to the brain by checkpointing reality, maintained custody of flesh vats containing humanoid bodies suspended in luminescent fluid, warned an entire party about dimensional time dilation while they were not listening, granted Markop titan-scale growth during the Spider Grove battle, conducted a transit ritual for Archie Miser while noting that Archie was absorbing too much power and then apparently allowed the ritual to proceed anyway, and is currently located somewhere in the Fracture Atrium of the Corvinarus Sanctum during a situation that is, by any measurable standard, catastrophic. Waluigi does not trust the Oracle. Waluigi has not trusted the Oracle from the beginning. The Oracle keeps being useful. This does not improve trust. If anything, consistent usefulness from an entity of uncertain identity and unknown motivation is MORE alarming than uselessness would be. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is going to document the Oracle with the same forensic precision he applies to every subject in this archive, which means documenting not only what the Oracle HAS done but what the Oracle has CHOSEN not to explain, because in Waluigi's extensive experience, the gap between what a powerful entity says and what it withholds is where the actual truth lives.

The Oracle is one of the most important figures in the Raventree crisis. The current archive entry does not reflect this. Waluigi is correcting that now.

## What The Oracle Claims To Be

The Oracle's self-description, assembled from multiple interactions across multiple sessions, is approximately as follows: a custodian of the timeline, responsible for maintaining the integrity of Raventree Manor's overlapping dimensional structure, racing to complete a Separation Ritual before the Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild can exploit the fractured planes for their own purposes.

This is a coherent explanation. It is also an explanation that conveniently justifies every action the Oracle has taken, every piece of information the Oracle has withheld, and every moment the Oracle has pushed the party toward a specific course of action. Waluigi notes that 'I am protecting the timeline' is the most flexible possible justification for behavior. It can explain help. It can explain harm. It can explain inaction when action was needed and action when inaction would have been safer. A custodian of the timeline can do anything and call it maintenance.

Waluigi has met people who claimed to be protecting larger structures before. The Mages' Guild claims to protect magical stability. The Regal Empire claims to protect order. These claims are not lies, exactly — the protection is real, the structure is real — but the protection always costs someone something, and the person paying is never the one making the claim.

What, exactly, is the timeline being protected FROM? And what is the Oracle willing to pay — in other people's suffering — to protect it?

## The Identity Question: Is The Oracle Orantha Cornelius?

The original builder of the Raventree Manor portal system was Orantha Cornelius. This name appears in fragmentary records connected to House Corvinarus — specifically as the architect of the extraplanar Sanctum that Bowser currently occupies. The Sanctum was described as 'a grand receiving area where privileged visitors to Darius' extraplanar Sanctum would enter through his portal,' which suggests the builder's name was Darius, not Orantha.

Waluigi notes the contradiction. The portal builder is named Darius in sanctum records. Orantha appears in other Corvinarus documentation. These may be two different people. They may be the same person under different names. Or one of them may be the Oracle.

What Waluigi knows: the Oracle has demonstrated knowledge of the sanctum's internal structure that goes far beyond what a visitor or student would have. The Oracle moved through the sanctum's spaces with the confidence of someone who designed them. The Oracle knew where the flesh vats were. The Oracle knew the ritual geometry. The Oracle knew which participants needed to stand in geometric opposition — Ice vs Force, Memory vs Chaos — as though the Oracle had designed that geometry.

You do not know a building the way the Oracle knows the sanctum unless you BUILT it. Or unless you have spent so much time maintaining it that the distinction between builder and caretaker has dissolved.

If the Oracle is Orantha Cornelius — or is connected to the Corvinarus family bloodline through Orantha — then the Oracle's motivations for maintaining the manor's dimensional integrity are not abstract custodial duty. They are personal. The manor is the Oracle's FAMILY'S creation. The dimensional machinery is the Oracle's FAMILY'S project. And the man in the crystal tethers — described as 'likely a key figure of the bloodline, perhaps the original Orangus Cornelius or the architect of the Grafting' — is possibly the Oracle's FAMILY MEMBER, suspended in twenty years of agony as a living battery for the dimensional rift.

If this is true, the Oracle is not a neutral custodian. The Oracle is a family member trying to resolve a crisis of their own bloodline's making, using the party as instruments while carrying personal stakes that were never disclosed.

Waluigi finds this interpretation consistent with every interaction the Oracle has had with the party. A neutral custodian protects timelines. A FAMILY MEMBER protects legacies. The difference in motivation produces different decisions, and those different decisions would explain why the Oracle has been systematically useful in ways that serve the party's survival but consistently opaque in ways that serve something else.

## The Bullet Incident: When The Oracle Survived Green T

Waluigi must address this because it is the single most important data point about the Oracle's nature and nobody has given it the analysis it deserves.

Green T shot the Oracle in the head.

Green T is not an amateur. Green T is a former crime lord who ran organized criminal operations through tea service and curtains, who shot the Shadow Anchor from the children's table during a vampire dinner party while dodging bat monsters, who treats a flintlock pistol as a formal diplomatic tool and has the accuracy to back it up. When Green T shoots someone in the head, the person does not survive.

The Oracle survived.

The Oracle's response to surviving a bullet to the brain was to CHECKPOINT REALITY. Not to dodge. Not to shield. Not to heal. To checkpoint. To establish a saved state of existence that the bullet could not retroactively violate.

Waluigi needs everyone to understand what this implies. Checkpointing reality is not a defensive spell. It is not a ward or a barrier or a healing ability. It is a TEMPORAL FUNCTION. The Oracle treated their own potential death the same way a scribe treats an important document — by saving a copy before the damage could reach it. The Oracle has sufficient control over the local timeline to define moments as CANONICAL and moments as NOT CANONICAL, and the moment of their death is, apparently, NOT CANONICAL.

This is not a power that an ordinary custodian possesses. This is not a power that most beings with names and bodies and addresses possess. This is the power of something that has existed in intimate relationship with time long enough that time has begun to extend professional courtesies.

How long has the Oracle been doing this? How many deaths have they checkpointed? Is the Oracle currently the ORIGINAL Oracle, or is the Oracle currently a checkpointed version of an Oracle who died at some point — possibly multiple points — and kept resuming from a saved state?

Waluigi does not know. The Oracle has not volunteered this information. But Waluigi notices that the Oracle does not seem particularly troubled by the experience of being shot, which suggests either extraordinary composure or extensive familiarity with the process of not dying when something tries to kill you.

Waluigi finds both possibilities deeply concerning.

## The Flesh Vats: What The Oracle Keeps

The Oracle maintains a collection of flesh vats.

Waluigi documented this in the Planar Sanctum article, but it bears emphasis here because the flesh vats are not separate from the Oracle's identity — they are part of it. The Oracle chose to build or inherit or maintain those vats. The Oracle showed them to Archie. The Oracle said, in explicit terms: 'If we do the ritual, we won't have to end up in a vat like this.'

The phrasing is important. Not 'you won't end up in a vat.' WE. The Oracle included itself in the population of entities that could theoretically end up in a vat, which implies either that the Oracle is vulnerable to the same institutional machinery that produced the vats, or that the Oracle was using 'we' rhetorically to create solidarity with Archie.

Waluigi notes that the vats contained 'malformed' humanoid bodies — 'flesh open with weeping sores, limbs ending prematurely, metal tubes impaling their flesh and extending down their open mouths.' A disposal chute handled the failed experiments.

These are not empty vats. These are OCCUPIED vats. People are currently in them. The Oracle knows this. The Oracle has been in proximity to this for long enough to use them as a rhetorical device in a conversation about motivation.

Waluigi's question, which nobody has answered: did the Oracle BUILD the vat infrastructure, INHERIT it, or OPPOSE it? Is the Oracle maintaining the vats as part of the larger Corvinarus dimensional machinery, or is the Oracle in the same position as the party — aware of the vats, unable to immediately stop them, working toward a solution that requires surviving long enough to implement it?

Archie left Bones in the Oracle's care with strict instructions not to put Bones in a flesh vat. The Oracle agreed. Waluigi notes that 'agreeing not to put someone in a flesh vat' is a very different commitment from 'not having the capacity to put someone in a flesh vat.' The Oracle CAN. The Oracle agreed not to. This is a meaningful distinction.

Bones is currently in the Oracle's care. In a collapsing library. In a dimension where time moves differently and portals close behind you.

Waluigi is monitoring this situation with the specific anxiety of someone who has documented too many cases where 'I agreed not to do the terrible thing' eventually became 'circumstances required the terrible thing.'

## The Separation Ritual: What The Oracle Needs

The Oracle's stated goal is the completion of a Separation Ritual — a procedure to sever the bleeding timelines and restore the dimensional integrity of Raventree Manor and its associated planar fragments.

The ritual requires twelve participants standing in geometric opposition. Ice versus Force. Memory versus Chaos. The participants must stand in precise positions within the ritual circle, and the arrangement is not arbitrary — it is a functional geometry, each pairing chosen to create tension between opposing metaphysical forces that, in balance, stabilize the dimensional boundary.

The Oracle warned the party explicitly that the ritual's mirror component would interrogate their truths. Any lies told within the circle would rupture it. This is either a designed safety feature — preventing destabilizing dishonesty from corrupting the spell — or a designed vulnerability that someone with knowledge of the ritual could exploit by feeding a participant false information to induce a lie.

Waluigi does not know which. The Oracle presented it as a warning. Warnings can also be instructions for people paying close enough attention.

The ritual requires blood to complete. The Oracle did not specify whose blood, what quantity, or what the blood is used for within the ritual's mechanism. Waluigi finds this omission significant. Rituals that require blood and decline to specify the details tend to require blood in quantities and from sources that the participants would object to if informed in advance.

The Oracle is racing the Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild. Both institutions have demonstrated interest in the Raventree dimensional structure — the Iron Legion seized the ritual room within hours of the Planar Fracture, and the Mages' Guild has been actively researching planar threading and accretion sites using what Archie described as 'Arcane Tethers.' The Oracle is terrified, by its own admission, that if the ritual fails, the timelines will not merely explode — they will MERGE into a mundane, easily conquerable reality.

Mundane reality. Easily conquerable.

Waluigi needs to sit with this phrase because it is the most politically revealing thing the Oracle has said in any documented interaction. The Oracle is not worried about suffering. The Oracle is not worried about death tolls or dimensional instability or the people currently suspended in flesh vats. The Oracle is worried about the resulting reality being CONQUERABLE.

By whom? The Iron Legion? The Mages' Guild? Or by something that the Oracle has not named, something that the merged mundane reality would be vulnerable to in ways that the current fractured dimensional structure is not?

Waluigi does not know. But an entity that prioritizes a reality's unconquerability over its livability has a very specific hierarchy of values, and that hierarchy is not the same as the party's.

## The Time Dilation: What The Oracle Knew and When

The Oracle informed Archie that a MONTH had passed in the Shadowfell since the planar fracture, while only days had passed in the Material Plane.

Waluigi needs to ask the question that nobody in the party appears to have asked: how long had the Oracle known this before telling Archie?

The Oracle moves through dimensional space as a professional function. The Oracle is a custodian of timelines. Time dilation across planar fragments is not a discovery — it is a known property of dimensional fragmentation that anyone with the Oracle's level of expertise would identify immediately upon the fracture's occurrence.

If the Oracle knew about the time dilation immediately — and Waluigi believes the Oracle did — then the Oracle chose when to disclose this information. The Oracle chose the specific moment of Archie's transit preparation to reveal that a month had passed for Green T, Bowser, and the Shadow Estate party. This means the Oracle calculated that this moment was the correct moment for that disclosure.

Why this moment and not earlier? What did Archie's reaction to the time dilation — his immediate demand to proceed with the transit despite the delay — accomplish that an earlier disclosure would not have? Did the Oracle need Archie in a specific emotional state before the transit? Did the Oracle need the transit to occur under specific conditions that Archie's urgency would produce?

Waluigi does not know. But the Oracle did not disclose the time dilation accidentally. The Oracle disclosed it deliberately, at a chosen moment, to produce a specific response.

This is what Waluigi means when he says he does not trust the Oracle. The Oracle is not lying. The Oracle provides accurate, useful information. But the Oracle provides it on a schedule that serves purposes the party cannot fully evaluate, because the purposes are never fully disclosed.

## The Transit Ritual: The Oracle Watched Archie Overload

When Archie stood in the ritual circle as the magical anchor for his transit to the Shadowfell, the Oracle said: 'It may be too powerful.'

Then the Oracle allowed the ritual to proceed.

Waluigi has thought about this more than is probably healthy. 'It may be too powerful' is not a statement that concludes with 'and therefore we proceed.' It is a statement that concludes with 'and therefore we stop and reassess.' If a surgeon opens a patient and says 'the tumor may be too close to the artery,' the surgery does not continue while the surgeon watches with wide eyes.

Unless the surgeon needed to see what would happen when the artery was nicked.

The Oracle has, by Waluigi's documented count, seen Archie's magic cause large-scale dimensional damage TWICE. The Planar Fracture was caused by Archie's entropy-bleeding magical signature destabilizing the synchronization ritual. The Oracle was warned about this, or was present for it, or both. And then, when Archie stood in a circle absorbing power for a solo dimensional transit, the Oracle noted that the power was too strong and allowed it to continue.

Waluigi's hypothesis: the Oracle needed to know what would happen when Archie's entropy-bleeding magic was concentrated and directed rather than ambient and reactive. The transit was a controlled experiment. Archie was the subject. The Oracle was the observer.

If Archie arrived in the Shadowfell safely, the Oracle gained information about controlled entropy-magic transit. If Archie arrived catastrophically — which, given that the Oracle said 'it may be too powerful' right before the session record ended, seems plausible — the Oracle gained different but equally valuable information about the upper limits of entropy-magic behavior.

Either way, the Oracle gained something.

What did Archie gain? A transit to a dimension he arrived at a month late, carrying enough volatile energy to potentially destabilize whatever was left of the Shadow Estate, with no idea where he was going because he specifically told the Oracle he had not 'a clue.'

## The Spider Grove Battle: The Oracle's Gift

During the Spider Grove engagement against the Arachnid Matriarch, the Oracle granted Markop titan-scale growth — scaling the centaur healer up to match the Matriarch's building-sized frame.

Waluigi documented this battle in the Markop article and will not repeat the full tactical analysis here. The relevant point is the Oracle's CHOICE in granting the ability.

The Oracle did not grant this ability to Archie, who has fire magic and would seem like the obvious choice for escalating a combat encounter. The Oracle did not grant it to Bowser, who is already the party's primary physical combatant. The Oracle granted it to MARKOP — the healer, the centaur, the person whose combat role is support and survival rather than offense.

Why Markop?

Waluigi has two theories. The first is tactical: Markop's centaur body at titan scale provides four-legged stability that a bipedal combatant like Archie or Bowser would not have. Four massive hooves can anchor against an opponent's struggle in ways that two legs cannot. The Oracle, who clearly thinks in spatial geometry, may have calculated that the centaur frame was the most efficient vessel for the titan ability in this specific engagement.

The second theory is more troubling: Markop is the party's structural support. The person everyone unconsciously orients toward when things go wrong. The quiet leader that the room turns to when screaming starts. If the Oracle understands group dynamics — and an entity that has been watching people for long enough to checkpoint its own death certainly understands group dynamics — then granting the power to Markop was not just a tactical decision. It was a SOCIAL one. Markop succeeding at titan scale, visibly, dramatically, in front of the party, reinforces Markop's role as the person the group trusts to handle impossible situations. It deepens the group's dependence on Markop's judgment.

Makop is also currently kidnapped in the grove, without his axe, and the party has fragmented partly because everyone expected Markop to be present and functional and he is not.

Waluigi does not know if the Oracle anticipated this. Waluigi suspects the Oracle anticipated more than it disclosed.

## The Oracle's Relationship With The Party: Selective Disclosure

Waluigi has assembled a list of things the Oracle has provided to the party:

- Information about time dilation (disclosed at the moment of Archie's transit preparation)
- Titan-scale growth for Markop (during Spider Grove battle)
- Healing for Archie (after Green T's bullet failed to kill the Oracle)
- Custody of Bones (reluctantly, with the qualifier 'quite a burden')
- Knowledge of the Separation Ritual's requirements (twelve participants, geometric opposition, blood required)
- Warning about the ritual's truth-interrogation property
- Warning about the Iron Legion and Mages' Guild's interests
- Transit ritual for Archie (completed while noting the power was too strong)

Waluigi has also assembled a list of things the Oracle has NOT provided:

- Its actual identity
- How it survived Green T's bullet
- How long it has been performing its custodial function
- The specific blood requirement for the Separation Ritual
- What 'easily conquerable reality' means and by whom
- The Oracle's personal stake in the ritual's outcome
- Whether the flesh vats are the Oracle's creation, inheritance, or opposition
- What happened to the original architect of the Sanctum
- Why it said 'it may be too powerful' and then proceeded with Archie's transit
- What it has been doing in the Fracture Atrium while Bowser fights the original Dan in a collapsing library

The ratio of disclosed to withheld is not the ratio of a trustworthy guide. It is the ratio of a person who has decided what the party needs to know in order to be useful to a project whose full scope has not been shared.

Waluigi respects the Oracle's information management. Waluigi would do the same thing in the Oracle's position. But Waluigi is documenting the gap because the gap is where the danger lives.

## The Current Situation: Oracle in the Atrium

The Oracle is currently somewhere in the Fracture Atrium of the Corvinarus Sanctum. The same complex where Bowser is stranded in a collapsing library with an unconscious original Dan, a sleeping copy Dan, Orange T, and Bones.

Bones is the person the Oracle agreed not to put in a flesh vat.

The flesh vats are presumably also somewhere in this complex, because the Oracle showed them to Archie during their visit to the Sanctum.

The Oracle is in the same complex as the person it agreed not to harm, the infrastructure for harming people it agreed not to use, and a situation that is deteriorating by the minute.

Waluigi notes that the Oracle has not visibly intervened in Bowser's situation. The Oracle has not closed the portal to bring Bowser back. The Oracle has not stabilized the collapsing floor. The Oracle has not provided Bowser with information about the original Dan's organizational connections or the significance of the Bowser Badge. The Oracle has not appeared to inform Bowser of the time dilation or the state of the party.

The Oracle has, as far as Waluigi's sources can determine, done nothing since Archie's transit.

This is either because the Oracle is occupied with something that requires its full attention in another part of the sanctum, or because the Oracle has decided that the current situation — Bowser stranded, Bones in a collapsing room, the party fragmented — serves some purpose that requires non-intervention.

Waluigi does not know which. Both are concerning.

## The Separation Ritual: What Happens If It Fails

The Oracle said the timelines would not just explode — they would merge into a mundane, easily conquerable reality.

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing this statement and has concluded that it is the most strategically important thing the Oracle has ever said, and nobody seems to have given it sufficient attention because they were busy with vampire dinner parties and shapeshifter executions and singing through a hostile grove.

Mundane reality is reality without the dimensional complexity that currently protects it. No overlapping planes. No Shadowfell reflection. No Feywild counterpart. No Deep Mirror layer. Just a single, flat, physically consistent reality with predictable rules and no hidden spaces.

For most people, this sounds like an IMPROVEMENT. Dimensional complexity is what produces the Planar Fracture, the time dilation, the flesh vats, the marriage contracts from vampire lords, and the experience of falling through a midnight portal into an extraplanar sanctum. A simpler reality sounds restful.

But Waluigi has spent enough time in institutions to understand what 'easily conquerable' means in practice. Dimensional complexity is defensive infrastructure. Multiple overlapping planes mean multiple possible escape routes, multiple possible hiding places, multiple angles from which a threat can be approached or avoided. The Iron Legion's greatest tactical weakness in the current crisis is that it cannot consistently project force across dimensional boundaries — the Shadowfell team survived partly because the Legion could not easily follow them, the Feywild team survived partly because the Legion could not operate effectively in fey space.

A mundane reality eliminates this. A mundane reality is a single theater of operations with no hidden dimensions. A mundane reality is exactly what the Iron Legion — with its standardized tactics, scalable deployment, and bureaucratic efficiency — is optimized to dominate.

The Oracle is not just trying to save the timelines. The Oracle is trying to maintain dimensional complexity as a strategic defense against a conquering power. The Separation Ritual is not a repair job. It is a FORTIFICATION.

Waluigi finds this interpretation both clarifying and alarming. It means the Oracle's priorities are geopolitical rather than humanitarian. The Oracle is not primarily concerned with the people currently in flesh vats, or the people killed when the Onyx Hand ran unchallenged for a month, or the party members who have been scattered across hostile dimensions. The Oracle is concerned with maintaining the architectural conditions that prevent a specific kind of conquest.

This is a legitimate goal. Waluigi is not saying it is not. But it is a goal that treats individual suffering as an acceptable cost of maintaining strategic complexity, and Waluigi wants that clearly documented.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Oracle is the most important unknown in the Raventree crisis. Not the most important FACTOR — the Iron Legion, the Mages' Guild, the Corvinarus succession, and the dimensional fracture all rank higher in terms of immediate causal impact. But the most important UNKNOWN. Everything else in the crisis is comprehensible. The Iron Legion wants to conquer. The Mages' Guild wants to control. The Corvinarus family is fractured between its living and undead branches. The House of Voss wants Remi for reasons that are predatory and documented.

The Oracle wants something that Waluigi cannot fully model. And things Waluigi cannot fully model are the things Waluigi worries about most.

Here is what Waluigi knows for certain:

The Oracle is old. Not elderly — old in the way that entities who have been checkpointing their own deaths and maintaining temporal custodianship across dimensional boundaries become old. Old in a way that changes the relationship between self-preservation and mission, where the mission has been running for so long that distinguishing between the two becomes difficult.

The Oracle is effective. Every action the Oracle has taken has produced a useful outcome for the party's survival, even when the method was alarming or the motivation was unclear. Green T's bullet should have ended a story. Instead it produced a lesson about the Oracle's nature. Archie's transit should have been refused or modified. Instead it produced information about entropy-magic behavior under directed conditions.

The Oracle is selective. Information is disclosed on a schedule that serves the Oracle's timeline rather than the party's. Trust is offered in increments calibrated to produce specific responses rather than genuine disclosure.

And the Oracle is PRESENT. In the Fracture Atrium. In the same complex as Bones, as Bowser, as the collapsing library, as the original Dan in critical condition. The Oracle is not distant, not evacuated, not safely removed from the immediate crisis. It is HERE.

Waluigi does not know if that is reassuring or terrifying.

Based on available evidence, Waluigi suspects it is both.

Waluigi survived the Feywild. Waluigi survived fairy courts and giant insects and Lady Aurelian's interminable riddle games. Waluigi survived because Waluigi is too stubborn to be destroyed by a dimensional catastrophe caused by people who did not listen to him.

Waluigi will also survive whatever the Oracle is planning.

And when the Oracle's full intention becomes clear — when the disclosure schedule reaches its final entry and the Separation Ritual either succeeds or fails and the blood requirement is finally explained — Waluigi will have it documented.

Every step. Every disclosed fact. Every withheld one.

Because Waluigi was watching from the beginning.

And Waluigi always notices.

WAH.

summary: Bones is a master infiltrator who survived Aegis Command, Order 120, and custody in the Corvinarus Planar Sanctum. After awakening alone in the Fractured Sanctum, Bones stole Fundamentals of Abjuration, uncovered Corvinarus's 10-page masterwork Veins of the Tapestry, refused the Oracle's flesh vat, engaged a fiendish Canoloth, was saved by the Toad God at the Astral Altar, and was teleported to the Regal Capital. Bones fled into a severe snowstorm and paid 3 Midland Ducats for shelter at an Alpine Inn. description:
Waluigi has to write about Bones carefully because Bones has lived through enough history to fill three separate war tribunals and still manages to walk into rooms nobody knew existed.

Originally one of the most capable operatives among the Liberated Toads, Bones achieved legend status by passing as an Iron Legion soldier inside Aegis Command for days. His capture triggered Order 120—the administrative execution of every Toad in Legion custody—a weight he has carried quietly ever since. But his story did not end in General Ironhand's interrogation room.

## Awakening in the Planar Sanctum
Following the shattered synchronization attempt with Archie Miser, Bones woke up alone on the black marble floor of the Planar Sanctum. Finding himself separated from Archie and wondering where Orange T had gone, Bones remembered Thornbury Bones and began exploring the crumbling complex. In the library, he spotted *Fundamentals of Abjuration*—a Mages' Guild Conservator text—and stole it directly from the Oracle's shelves, remarking he'd keep it when he found free time.

## Reading the Veins of the Tapestry
Near the scattered debris of a ruined grand turret—where a fallen belfry bell lay smashed against black marble—Bones found a second tome on the floor: *Veins of the Tapestry: A Record of Threads Severed and Mended*. Written in the precise, arrogant hand of Corvinarus, the pages whispered into his skull under the rippling light of nearby vats:

- **Page 1:** Dedication 'To the three who will break what we bound' signed with three interlocking threads (one frayed).
- **Page 2:** Architectural diagram of pre-Fracture Raventree Manor with mirror and shadow weak points.
- **Page 3:** Account of the 988 BF Grafting ritual, describing the egg's scream as 'the sound of a future being forced into existence.'
- **Page 4:** Warning about the Oracle (OC): 'pulls levers she does not fully understand... vats were never meant to birth keepers.'
- **Page 5:** List of test subjects from Orangus Cornelius to Vivian ('He laughs when cut. This was not planned.').
- **Page 6:** Circle repair instructions (bone ash, live wood, iron dust, chalk) and doodle of a three-eyed figure: 'Do not trust the fire that cannot burn.'
- **Page 7:** Shadowfell lament: 'Orangus believed order could contain the bleed... The Hand feeds what it claims to control.'
- **Page 8:** Pressed glowing Feywild flower with Lady Aurelian's warning: 'the present must be severed from the others or all will unravel like cheap silk.'
- **Page 9:** Map of Deep Mirror sanctum labeling abomination vats as 'Failed attempts at continuity' with 'Wrong lever' underlined three times.
- **Page 10:** Prophecy fragment: 'When the one-armed shadow walks with the fire that bleeds, and the green one takes the children's table, the threads will knot or snap. Choose the knot.'

## Confrontation with the Oracle & Flesh Vat Refusal
Hiding in turret rubble after hearing footsteps, Bones was confronted from behind by the Oracle. Apprehensive, Bones asked where they stood. The Oracle reprimanded Bones for failing to kill rival Oracles over the past two months and warned him never to touch his books. In the central chamber—flanked by Western violet and Eastern erratic orange Crystal Tethers surrounding a glass vat wrapped in lightning—the Oracle urged Bones into a flesh vat to reveal his 'true self-reflection.' Recognizing the red flag, Bones refused. When an unseen portal opened and Bones attempted to flee, the Oracle force-dragged him back.

## Combat with the Canoloth & The Astral Altar
A fiendish Canoloth appeared among floating space-time rocks. As the Oracle used a vibrating tuning fork to shift the beast in and out of reality, the Canoloth attacked Bones, snaring him with its spiny tongue and entangling both his longsword and vile mace. In agony, Bones grabbed the creature's tongue bare-handed, dragging the multi-ton yugoloth toward a cliff edge while demanding to kill it 'the actual way.' The Canoloth swiped Bones across the chest, knocking him unconscious.

Bones's mind was intercepted to the Astral Altar, where the Toad God (Mad Toad) greeted him as a 'best friend.' The Toad God advised Bones: 'Don't kill the Oracle, keep him alive. Leave the manor and crystal shard intact and leave it divided.' The Toad God mentioned being kept busy by 'pesky star bears wanting to give away their stars to a bunch of hooligans (the Oracle)' before a blinding light returned Bones to the sanctum floor.

The Oracle healed Bones, lecturing him that physical weightlifting won't grant strength if his mental reflex is to flee rather than fight. Agreeing to teleport Bones to a 'friend,' the Oracle placed him in a red circle pointed toward Alpine Bank.

## Eavesdropping at Alpine Bank & The Mountain Snowstorm
Materializing at Alpine Bank in the mountains near Mighdural (the Regal Capital), Bones met Thornbury. Lingering outside to eavesdrop on Thornbury's session with the Alpine banker, Bones learned:
- Thornbury operates with Iron Legion credentials and serves higher Legion commanders.
- The Legion considers Bones a wanted criminal for allegedly 'strangling a toad to death on the Vigilance.'
- Thornbury placed an official bounty on Archie Miser to collect 2,062 gold for the broken hempen rope debt.

Realizing Thornbury was a traitor, Bones quietly slipped out into a brewing mountain snowstorm. Freezing in the blizzard, he was escorted by local guards to an Alpine Inn, where he paid 3 Midland Ducats (3 gold) for a room upstairs, keeping a watchful eye for spies as he collapsed into bed.

## 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — The Locked Cottage and the Goblin Camp
A later field account begins after an unexplained gap from Bones's tree-rest beyond the Legion wall. He wakes in a locked cottage with two armed Toad guards, tries a key swipe that fails, then presses an emergency-release button that opens every door. The guards call his confinement a “bonding ritual”; the phrase does not establish consent or explain how he arrived.

Outside, Bones sees an unnamed green-cloaked figure near someone called Mimbus, then becomes caught in Fawful's forest operation. A hypno-helmet drone attacks an unnamed person; an older woman and a fox-eared Toad help remove it. The conversation invokes the Emerald Enclave and a plan to stop a dragon-linked ritual, but its membership, the fox-eared Toad's identity, and the dragon's identity remain unverified. The words “Konathin” and “Toad ie Fox” are not reconciled with roster entry #73; Toad ie Foxx remains listed as unseen.

Bones accepts a recorded 20-gold payment, takes an unnamed guard's outer clothes but leaves the shorts, and escapes through a broken window. Fawful's sacrifice preparations and a separate mustard-spraying clockwork drone drive him into the trees. At an unnamed goblin camp, a fart-spray gag is recorded without a clear user or target. A figure called an “Archie bot” puts out a fire with “WATERBALL!” and is recruited. A dragon later leaves with an Archie-like passenger. Neither is equated with Archie Miser, and the dragon is not equated with The Supplied Dragon. Bones declines the dragon's invitation, sleeps in trees, and spends one hour measuring a map whose route, scale, origin, and destination are not transcribed.

The event files a 900-XP preview; the authoritative ledger is unchanged until the table confirms it.

## The Full Field Record
The short version of Bones's file hides the most important truth: he is not merely a survivor who happened to be present when the Iron Legion committed a massacre. He is a player-character who repeatedly chose the dangerous route because the safe route left somebody else behind. The ledger records him across the Spider Grove, the Vigilance, Aegis Command, Raventree Manor, the Feyward, the Shadowfell, the Planar Sanctum, and the mountain road. The dates do not always agree—planes and loops have made chronology unreliable—but the decisions do.

### Before the Capture: The Operative Who Kept Going Back
Bones worked with the Liberated Toads as an infiltrator, scout, and field survivor. He passed through hostile spaces by disguising himself, reading a room before entering it, and keeping an exit in mind. His record includes the first night at Raventree Manor, the Mazebound Grove, the Spider Grove, and the Solarium Detonation. In the grove campaign he helped the party survive a nest full of coordinated spiders and a matriarch whose hoard was almost as dangerous as the webbing. During the Solarium operation, the party's explosive shortcut destroyed the floor and turned a victory into another structural emergency. Bones's contribution is often recorded as “named in the battle record,” but that phrasing understates the player behind it: he was one of the people still moving when the map stopped behaving like a map.

The Vigilance Crisis and Iron Sky Breach made that skill political. When the mobile headquarters was attacked, the Liberated Toads lost their ship, their communications center, and their sense that distance could protect them. Bones stayed in the field while the movement fractured. At Aegis Command he used a guard disguise to enter the fortress and look for Speaker L. The prisoner was a decoy. General Marcus Ironhand exposed Bones, stabbed him, and issued Order 120: the immediate execution of Toad prisoners. Bones's infiltration did not cause the Legion's decision to murder its prisoners; it revealed how ready the Legion already was to do it. The massacre made his name part of the war's public record.

### Order 120 and the Reclamation
The Aegis Command riot turned a covert war into an open one. Bones's survival, the prisoners' deaths, and the escape toward the Whispering Caves changed Speaker L from a political voice into a war leader. The later reclamation of the Vigilance returned the ship to Toad control, but not the old world. Bones belongs to the generation of the Liberated Toads who learned that a successful mission can still end with a ship lost, a friend captured, and a faction forced to choose between negotiation and retaliation.

### Raventree: Captured, Rescued, and Captured Again
At Raventree Manor, Bones was present for the first-night panic, the haunted grounds, the unstable portals, and the Battle of the Brobot. The Brobot engagement is not a clean victory: Mr. L emerged as the Green Thunder, grabbed Bones, and treated him as a hostage while Archie’s magic went out of control and the manor collapsed around the combatants. Bones was knocked unconscious and taken for “healing”—or, as the first wording put it, “sealed up.” The Mages' Guild's containment procedures were already prepared. That detail matters. Bones was not simply unlucky; powerful institutions had begun planning around the possibility that people like him would resist them.

The surrounding testimony adds further pressure. The Medical Extortion incident records Bones as chemically held in an arcane coma while the Legion used his condition as leverage. The Ruined Manor Convergence and the Shadeward ritual left him as the person who had been taken while Archie crossed planes. The records disagree about exactly when he was conscious, but they agree that custody was used as a tool. Bones's status is therefore “Active,” not “safe”: active means his story is unresolved and his choices are still capable of changing the campaign.

### The Fracture, the Telescope, and the Cost of Being Left Behind
The Grove of Woe split the party across planes. The Shadow Estate, the Telescope and Tennis Match, and the later Sanctum records describe a campaign where bodies, memories, and timelines stopped arriving together. Bones was listed as comatose, left in the Oracle's care, treated by Orange T, and discussed as someone who might be “from the future.” Those labels are not a diagnosis. They are the language other people used while trying to locate him.

When the telescope sequence showed the party that the past could be watched but not safely corrected, Bones's file became a continuity problem. He was not present for every scene, but his capture, his absence, and the uncertainty about whether he could be restored shaped the decisions of Archie, Remi, Waluigi, and the Toads. This is why mention-only records do not raise his Power score: being discussed is not the same as acting. The ledger gives Bones power credit only for four confirmed special events, while still preserving the larger history around him.

### Awakening in the Planar Sanctum
After the failed synchronization with Archie, Bones woke alone on black marble in the Fractured Planar Sanctum. He did not know where Archie or Orange T had gone. He did know that he was alive, that the complex was unstable, and that a library full of dangerous answers was within reach. He stole *Fundamentals of Abjuration* from the Oracle's shelves, then found Corvinarus's ten-page *Veins of the Tapestry* beside the fallen belfry bell.

The book gave Bones information worth more than a weapon: the 988 BF Grafting ritual, the weak points of Raventree Manor, the Oracle's unfinished relationship with the vats, the list of test subjects, the ingredients for repairing a circle, the Shadowfell's failure to contain the bleed, Lady Aurelian's warning, the failed continuity vats, and the prophecy of the one-armed shadow, the bleeding fire, and the green one at the children's table. Bones read the entire record while reality moved around him. He understood enough to know that the prophecy was not a promise of safety.

When the Oracle found him, Bones negotiated, apologized, concealed the stolen books, and asked what he could do. The answer was another impossible assignment: kill the other Oracles. The Oracle then offered him a flesh vat and promised a “true self-reflection.” Bones recognized the offer as a trap and refused. This is a defining player decision. He did not reject knowledge; he rejected surrendering authorship of his identity to an institution that stored people in tanks.

### The Canoloth Trial and the Toad God
The Canoloth fight proved the difference between being armed and being prepared. Bones fired and missed. The creature's tongue wrapped around his longsword and vile mace. Instead of abandoning the weapons, he seized the tongue with his hands, dragged the fiend toward the cliff, and demanded that it be killed “the actual way.” The creature struck him unconscious.

His mind then reached the Astral Altar, where the Toad God called him a best friend and gave him strategically inconvenient advice: keep the Oracle alive, leave the manor and crystal shard intact, and leave the shard divided. The Toad God also spoke of star bears and hooligans. Bones returned healed, but not unchanged. The Oracle's lesson—that lifting weights is not the same as becoming mentally stronger—landed because Bones already understood the cost of panic. His strength is not a clean stat block. It is the decision to keep acting after fear has supplied a reasonable argument for stopping.

### Alpine Bank, Thornbury, and the Mountain Road
The Oracle sent Bones to Alpine Bank near Mighdural. Bones arrived without a reliable map and immediately used the skill that has kept him alive: he stayed outside and listened. From Thornbury and the banker he learned that Thornbury had Iron Legion credentials, that the Legion considered Bones wanted for allegedly strangling a Toad on the Vigilance, and that Archie carried a 2,062-gold bounty over a broken hempen rope. Bones did not confront Thornbury. He left with the information.

A mountain blizzard followed. Bones froze, was escorted by guards to an Alpine Inn, paid three Midland Ducats for a room, and watched for spies instead of sleeping normally. The next stage carried him through the snow toward Arunedeal. He asked for work, tried to find a blacksmith, tested whether the guards were lying, and ran when the situation turned bad. He met the goblin Naaook, misunderstood his name as “Zook,” negotiated for a winter coat and shield, and paid seventy-five gold after briefly trying to reduce the price to fifty.

At the camp he met a battle-worn Toad speaking Draconic. The Toad accepted the armor and tools Bones had acquired, then used a staff to release tiny fey spirits that drove off hostile goblins. Bones called him “Elbow,” demanded an introduction, warned him not to betray him, and agreed to travel together without admitting that this was a team. Their partnership is not sentimental. It is a field alliance built on survival, suspicion, and the recognition that a lone operative cannot solve every checkpoint.

The pair then reached an Iron Legion fortress wall blocking the mountain pass. Bones assessed the position correctly: he was willing to fight, but not to lose. He turned away from a frontal assault. That retreat is not cowardice and it is not a victory. It is the level-five decision of a player who has already seen what happens when a single infiltration becomes an excuse for an army to execute prisoners.

### Present Status and Unresolved Questions
Bones's last confirmed stop at the Alpine mountain inn is no longer current. The 2 Aethel field account ends with him in the trees, wearing a borrowed Bean disguise and holding a map he measured for one hour; the later 4–5 Aethel medical-extortion record describes him in a chemically induced coma. No recovery or current location is confirmed. The session's 900-XP award is a preview only; the authoritative ledger remains **Level 5, 7,880 XP, 6,120 XP from Level 6**, with 23 entries until the table confirms the awards. His Power is 8 (Veteran), based on a base 4 and four confirmed special-event boosts—not on every rumor attached to his name. His Fame is 52 (Known), with a public signal reduced by the infamy associated with Disaster Inc. and the Legion's wanted notice.

His immediate questions are practical. Is Elbow an ally, a lure, or another person being used by a larger faction? What did Thornbury report after Bones escaped? What is the Legion actually seeking beyond the checkpoint? Does *Veins of the Tapestry* describe Bones's future, or merely recognize the kind of person the crisis requires? What is Bones's real name, and why has he never thought of one? The file does not resolve these questions. It preserves them because a player character is not finished when the archive becomes confident.

**Waluigi's ruling:** Bones is not an NPC waiting for a quest giver to assign him purpose. He is an active level-five infiltrator whose choices have caused discoveries, changed battlefields, exposed institutional violence, preserved forbidden knowledge, and created alliances that no faction authorized. The next entry belongs to him.

faiths.note: Bones stole Fundamentals of Abjuration and read Corvinarus's ten-page Veins of the Tapestry — a masterwork that treats the structure of reality as a text with an author. Gematria Gnosis holds that the sublime is reachable through the horrific and abstract. Bones took the reading and left the reverence.

description:
Waluigi has been putting off this record because writing it requires admitting how little the archive has.

Here is the whole of it. Orange T is an orange Toad. He treats the wounded — Bones in the sanctum library, competently and without being asked. He carries a healer's staff. He is on friendly terms with [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik). He is not, by his own flat statement, an Oracle. And he is never observed entering a room.

That last point is not a joke. In the sanctum a violent, alert, extremely large person fought a Mages' Guild operative to within an inch of his life, finished, looked up — and Orange T was there, and had been there throughout, treating a comatose man in the corner with the comfortable familiarity of someone who had established routines.

## The banishment, which was not an accident

Orange T asked Bowser whether he cared what was done with the two unconscious Dans. Bowser, exhausted, said 'not particularly.' Both Dans were banished immediately. Bowser's objection arrived while the Shadowfell Dan was already disappearing. Orange T said 'oh oops.'

Waluigi has documented enough manipulation to recognise the shape of this one. The question was casual, the consent was imprecise, and the spell was ready. A man who needed permission obtained permission from someone too tired to parse what he was granting.

## What the archive does not know

How he travels. Why he was in the sanctum. What he wants with the Dans. Whether 'I'm a friend of Hjumpik' is true, and whether Hjumpik would say the same sentence back. He pointed at something invisible and laughed when Bowser could not see it. He identified Bones as 'from the future' and 'no one important' in consecutive sentences. He implied Bowser had a mission involving other Oracles that Bowser knew nothing about.

**Not to be confused with [Mystic Morel](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mystic_morel), Purple T** — a different Toad entirely, who works the Feyward and robs people. The archive has already made that mistake once and is noting it here so it does not happen again.

WAH.
